questions.question: Why does this MR exist? What does it change for API users?
questions.answer: It adds Redis-backed rate limiting to POST /orders (20 requests per minute per IP, returning 429 with Retry-After), and also publishes an order.created event, computes order totals from a pricing service instead of a constant, and removes the unused legacy in-memory throttle.

questions.question: What is the main risk or thing a reviewer should scrutinize?
questions.answer: The limiter depends on Redis on the request path and uses a fixed window keyed by req.ip, so it allows bursts at window boundaries, may mis-key clients behind a proxy, and a Redis outage would break or block order creation (no failure handling).

questions.question: What happens when a client sends more than 20 requests in a minute, and what happens to the key?
questions.answer: The 21st request in the window gets HTTP 429 with body {error: rate_limited} and a Retry-After header of the window in seconds. The key is rl:<ip>:<window number>; it gets an expiry set (pexpire) only when the count is 1.

questions.question: Where does the limiter live and where is it wired in?
questions.answer: The middleware is the rateLimit function in src/api/rate-limit.ts, mounted in src/api/server.ts on the /orders path with windowMs 60000 and max 20.

questions.question: What design question should a reviewer raise about the limiter or the new order flow?
questions.answer: Increment and expire are two separate Redis calls (INCR then PEXPIRE), so a crash between them leaves a key with no TTL; also the event is published after the DB insert with no outbox, so a publish failure after insert loses the event, and the limit is hardcoded rather than configurable.
must_mention: INCR and PEXPIRE are separate non-atomic calls
event publish is not atomic with the DB insert

questions.question: Which tests does this MR add or change, what scenarios do they cover, and what important case is untested?
questions.answer: No tests are added or changed in this MR. The most important untested behavior is the rate limiter itself: requests over 20 per minute getting 429 with Retry-After, and the behavior when Redis fails or is unavailable (the middleware has no error handling).

questions.question: List the files this MR changes in a meaningful way and say in a few words what changed in each.
questions.answer: src/api/rate-limit.ts: new Redis-backed fixed-window rate limit middleware returning 429 with Retry-After; src/api/server.ts: applies rateLimit (20 per 60s) to /orders and publishes order.created after creating an order; src/services/orders.ts: createOrder rejects empty orders, prices items via priceFor, and stores status pending; src/queue/events.ts: new publish function that only logs the topic and payload; src/legacy-throttle.ts: deleted unused in-memory throttle; docs.md: README.md renamed to docs.md with a rate limit sentence added
